resources.string: Root mode uses a tightly limited UID 0 service and requires Magisk, KernelSU, APatch, or another compatible su manager. Shizuku mode uses the standard ADB/Shizuku service. You can change this later.
NR only can leave the phone without calls, SMS, or data when standalone 5G is unavailable. Use 5G preferred for daily use.
Show VoWiFi Roaming preference in Settings
Show IMS Status in SIM Info
Monitoring is read-only and separate. Choose a SIM below to open every IMS, 5G, LTE+, radio, CarrierConfig, expert, and band control.
No active SIM is available. Return to Home and confirm privileged access.
Use Automatic/NSA preference for normal use. SA-only and manual bands can remove calls, SMS, or data where the selected network is unavailable.
VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR, NSA/SA architecture, radio mode, IMS restart, CarrierConfig, expert settings, and reset controls.
Easy Mode, LTE carrier aggregation, Auto/Force NSA/Force SA, root-force diagnostics, and selectable LTE/NR bands.

Capture 24 timestamped snapshots over two minutes while you move through a known 5G area. The report records NRARFCN and calculated NR frequency, SS/CSI metrics, registration and reject state, callbacks, PCC/SCC changes, Android gates, regional-patch hashes, modem carrier-profile IDs, baseband/build-carrier properties, and sanitized start/end CarrierConfig, phone-process, registry, physical-channel, and radio-log evidence.
The field-test report could not be created.
The report excludes phone numbers, IMSI, and ICCID. It includes tower cell IDs and radio details, which can reveal approximate location; review it before sharing publicly.

For two minutes, opens every supported Android-side LTE/NR gate, requests Automatic bands where supported, keeps the data connection active with small connectivity checks, and captures the full field-test report. Previous settings are restored automatically.

Experimental test only. It cannot lower tower-controlled attach thresholds or create signal. It temporarily changes radio policy, uses a small amount of mobile data, and may increase battery use. Do not use during an emergency call.

Keep the phone near the target site and mobile data enabled. The app will temporarily open supported LTE/NR gates and generate small network requests for two minutes, then restore the captured settings even if you stop the test.
Aggressive test active; keep the screen open and move through the target area.
Some temporary gates were rejected: %1$s. Capturing the available evidence.
Aggressive test finished and the pre-test settings were restored.
The test ended, but Android rejected part of the rollback. Use Restore all and reboot from the power icon.
New here? Read the safe workflow before changing IMS, radio profiles, or bands.

Choose Root or Shizuku, confirm the privileged service and SIM are detected, then check IMS registration for each SIM. Use FIX only when IMS is unavailable and you want Google/carrier defaults restored.

Open IMS & 5G controls for VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR and NSA/SA settings. Open Band selection & LTE+ for Easy Mode, radio preference, carrier aggregation and advanced bands. Keep Automatic bands unless you know your carrier’s deployed bands.
Use Live, 5G attach trace, PCC/SCC, CarrierConfig diff and NR capabilities to inspect the network. Root exposes deeper phone-process evidence; Shizuku pages clearly mark unavailable privileged data.

Standard mode records two minutes without changing settings. Aggressive mode temporarily opens supported LTE/NR gates and sends small connectivity checks, then automatically rolls back. Share the generated text report when reporting a device or carrier problem.

If a manual band or SA-only setting removes service, use Undo when offered. The power icon restores all app-managed SIM settings and reboots. Remove the root regional modem patch before a firmware update, then validate it again afterward.

Pixel IMS 5G cannot amplify RF signal, create tower coverage, lower network-controlled attach thresholds, bypass subscriber authorization, or guarantee 5G/VoWiFi. Root-only modem changes remain unavailable through Shizuku.
IWLAN is the IMS-over-Wi-Fi transport, not cellular band 1800. This monitor shows Wi-Fi frequency, IMS transport, and the LTE/NR anchor separately.
Serving and nearby cells reported by Android
The modem/Android framework did not expose any cells in this scan.
This enables compatible Android flags and keeps bands automatic. It cannot add IMS entitlement, an IMEI allow-list entry, or tower support.
Profile applied; IMS was restarted. Watch the live IMS transport above.
Android or the modem rejected part of the profile.

Nearby-cell results are the complete set Android exposes to this app, not every transmitter on the air. Tensor modem firmware and carrier policy may hide cells, CA component carriers, or rejected NR candidates.
Enables VoLTE, enhanced LTE/LTE+, automatic bands, LTE+NR allowance, and requests Tensor modem CA for this SIM.
Easy Mode is managing radio settings. Switch it off to unlock advanced controls.
Easy Mode enabled: VoLTE and the Tensor CA node are enabled. LTE+ appears when the carrier schedules aggregation.
Easy Mode enabled. VoLTE and LTE+ configuration are applied; direct CA verification is unavailable on this modem build.
Easy Mode is off. Advanced controls are unlocked; the enabled calling settings are left in place.
The modem or Android rejected part of the Easy Mode request. Advanced controls remain unlocked.
Automatic — modem and carrier band selection
Green always means the modem currently reports signal on that band, including in Automatic mode. Normal color means the band can be selected, but no signal is currently reported.
The modem retained the band selection
The modem rejected this band restriction and remains on Automatic
No restriction assumed; this Pixel modem does not expose live band readback
Android or the selected privilege mode rejected a modem read. The page will stay open, and supported controls can still be tried safely. Include the technical detail below when reporting this device.
Enter valid comma-separated positive band numbers
Selecting unsupported bands can remove service. Multiple LTE bands allow CA candidates, but the modem and carrier—not this app—choose the actual aggregation combination.
Common LTE bands: 1, 3, 7, 8, 20, 28, 38, 40, 41. Edit this list for your carrier before applying.
Enabled (the carrier decides when to aggregate)
Bands detected in active radio scan
NSA attachment is available from the serving LTE cell
NR is advertised, but the serving LTE cell does not allow EN-DC/NSA attachment
The serving cell does not currently advertise NR
Modem preference applied; the network can still reject registration
The modem rejected the requested radio mode
Forcing changes the modem preference and allowed radio types. It cannot create EN-DC support or override carrier authentication and network registration.
Local 5G force is active for this SIM
Not exposed by this Android build
All readable Android-side LTE/NR gates are open. The modem will attach when the network offers and accepts NR.
Root force was only partly applied. Rejected: %1$s
The exact pre-force radio masks, band selection, NR modes, and debug properties were restored.
Part of the root-force snapshot could not be restored. Use Restore all and reboot from About.
5G is connected. The network and modem accepted NR.
The LTE anchor advertises EN-DC, so NSA attachment is locally possible.
At least one Android or carrier configuration gate still blocks LTE/NR.
All local gates are open, but the modem exposes no usable NR cell and the LTE anchor reports no EN-DC. Root cannot create a tower signal.
The cell advertises NR, but the modem is not attached. Coverage, SIM provisioning, modem policy, or network rejection may be responsible.
Android is not exposing enough modem state to prove why NR is not attached.

Root Force snapshots the current state, removes band restrictions, enables NSA + SA in CarrierConfig, opens every readable allowed-network reason, enables IMS debug gates, and restarts IMS. It does not write modem NV/EFS. Device-specific NV profiles must match the exact Pixel model and baseband.

Experimental systemless Tensor modem patch. It copies this firmware’s own cfg.db, validates the SQLite schema and integrity, and maps only wildcard/PTCRB carrier entries to the firmware’s permissive profile. It does not fake the SIM country, registered PLMN, or Wi-Fi regulatory country.

Root and Magisk only. A reboot is required. Before applying a firmware update, remove this patch and reboot; after the update, validate and install a fresh copy. The installer refuses unknown layouts. This can open a local modem profile but cannot bypass Dialog authentication, tower EN-DC configuration, subscriber entitlement, or RF hardware limits.
Root mode with Magisk is required. This operation is unavailable through Shizuku.

Applies every reversible Android-side regional gate available to the Shizuku shell: LTE + NR network policy, NSA + SA CarrierConfig, VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR, LTE+ and IMS visibility. It requests Automatic bands where the modem API supports it, then reads the effective regional gates back.
Android-side Shizuku gates are open. Test near the 5G site.
Android-side Shizuku gates are open. Automatic band reset is unavailable on this modem, so the existing band selection was left unchanged.

Important: this is not the Tensor cfg.db modem patch that made 5G work in the root comparison. Android 17 blocks UID 2000 from installing a vendor/Magisk overlay. If the modem profile still rejects EN-DC after these gates pass, the same modem fix still requires root.
The app will validate and stage a systemless vendor carrier database overlay. The change becomes active after reboot. If service becomes unstable, return here, schedule removal, and reboot.
Magisk will remove the systemless overlay during the next reboot and restore the stock firmware database.
The last app action was “%1$s”. That restriction may have removed every usable network. Revert that exact change?
The SIM has no cellular service. IMS cannot register until LTE or NR service returns.
The active carrier configuration reports VoLTE as unavailable.
The current allowed-network mask excludes both LTE and NR, which IMS voice requires on Tensor Pixels.

LTE/NR service and the local VoLTE flag are available, but the carrier has not accepted IMS registration. SIM provisioning, the carrier IMS server, roaming policy, or an IMEI allow-list may be responsible.
Android could not read enough telephony state to identify the failure.

This clears every carrier override, band restriction, forced radio profile, and saved recovery state created by Pixel IMS 5G for all active SIMs, then reboots the phone. It does not factory-reset the phone.
Report a bug or send feedback
Downloading version %1$s; Android will ask you to approve installation
Notifies you when a new signed Pixel IMS 5G release is available.
Update now? Download and install it securely inside Pixel IMS 5G.
Pixel IMS 5G can periodically check GitHub Releases and notify you once when a newer signed APK is available.
Download paused; Android will resume it automatically.
Download failed (code %1$d). Tap Download again to retry.
Allow Pixel IMS 5G to install this signed update, then return to continue.
Android could not open the downloaded APK. Open Downloads and select the Pixel IMS 5G update.
Based on the original GPL Pixel IMS project by kyujin-cho and its community contributors.
Wildcard/PTCRB Tensor cfg.db mapping research credited to the Pixel Modem Fix and Displax modem-fix projects. Pixel IMS 5G independently validates and patches the current firmware database.
